title: The Fox and the Crow
logline: A hungry fox climbs to a crow's nest with sweet words of friendship, hoping she will fetch him food; the wary crow answers every promise with a reason not to trust him, and he goes home alone, beaten by a better mind.
moral: Judge an offer of friendship by what the friend has done, not by what he says; and know the limits of your own strength.
tone: A dry comedy of manners on a mountain top: a charming liar whose belly, tongue and shadow keep giving him away, and a small calm bird who is never fooled. Light, never cruel; the fox ends rueful, not punished.

beats.summary: The fox is hungry: empty bone, growling belly.
High above, the crow lands on her nest among the rocks (crane up the mountain).
The fox's thought: the crow can reach food he cannot. A plan forms.
He offers friendship: a heart floats over the chasm.
Mask off: in his private thought the food outweighs the heart.
'You hunt birds': his shadow on the rock shows the hunter.
'Pretty words are not enough': she bursts the heart.
He tries a tale: the flea and the mouse who helped each other.
She knows his past: he tricked the wolf who lived with him.
Her tale of the old falcon who turned from force to trickery.
The falcon's smile and the fox's smile are the same: SAME TRICK.
The sparrow who copied the eagle is stuck in the wool.
The warning: know your limit, stay away from my nest.
The fox leaves, sad and then angry.
He admits it: she is craftier than he is.
He returns alone to his cave, still hungry.

sets.description: The planned rockyHill, built tall for this film: one world 1000 wide x 2300 high, a bare grey rock mountain (the grey of the Library den rock, blue Ben-Day shading on the left faces, black brush outline, a few crack lines and dry tufts). FOOT: ground y 2100 (Library ground colours), cave mouth a navy arch x 200..460, 230 high, in the rock face (same drawing style as the Library den arch; den's bones on the ground, one bone as a prop). RAMPS: ledge A y 1700 (x 480..1000), ledge B y 1300 (x 0..540), drawn as flat steps with a pale top edge; they are only passed by the crane and are the path the fox takes. TOP: terrace y 900, x 0..600, with a rock wall behind its left part (x 60..330, y 480..900, flat pale grey, used for the hunter shadow); CHASM x 600..690, dark navy, falling out of view; nest PINNACLE x 690..890, flat top y 610, with the Library nest at (790, 610) between two small standing rocks (x 700 and 880, 70 high). Above y 480 open sky. Sky by skyCycle, drawn in panel space behind the world: u 0.12 at the start, 0.25 by S5, 0.38 in S11, 0.46 in S12. All numbers are the design; adjust by eye on the first stills.

props.description: Library nest with 3 eggs at (790, 610); the crow perches on its rim.
Library heart: the fox's offer of friendship. First heart r 34 (burst at 57.54), second r 44 (sinks into the chasm at 142.44); small copies in clouds.
Library fig: the food in the fox's thoughts.
Library worm: the small birds' food in the falcon tale.
One clean bone (the Library den bone drawing reused as a movable prop, 70 long); also the shared bone in the wolf memory (110 long with a little red meat).
Planned coinPile: a mound of 12 yellow discs (r 12, black outline, red dot shading), one coin can be taken.

Simple side-view sheep: wool body from 7 overlapping white circles (about 200 x 130), black face and four thin legs, a chew field and a head turn; two wool curls that can hold a bird's feet. A copy at s 0.45 is the lamb.
Small grey stones (r 5..9) that fall into the chasm with fallY.

scenes.summary: Morning at the foot of a bare grey mountain. The thin fox comes out of his cave, his belly growls, he finds only a clean bone. Then the camera cranes up the whole rock face to the top, where the crow lands on her nest between the rocks.

scenes.summary: The crow's careful answer. 'You hunt birds': on the rock wall behind the smiling fox his shadow shows a hunter with open jaws. 'I could be your prey': she shrinks, and his tongue slips out by itself. 'How can I trust you?' 'Pretty words are not enough': she pecks the floating heart and it bursts.

scenes.summary: The crow has listened but is not persuaded: she sweeps the story cloud away with a wing. 'Friends may help each other, but you tricked a wolf who lived with you.' Her memory cloud (blue) shows the fox and a wolf sharing the cave; while the wolf sleeps the fox creeps away with their bone. The real fox sweats. 'How would I be safe near you?' She points at the gap that protects her.

subtitles.ar: كان ثعلب يعيش في كهف على جبل، ويعاني الجوع كثيرًا.|وكان فوق الجبل غراب له عش بين الصخور.|فكر الثعلب أن الغراب يستطيع الوصول إلى طعام لا يستطيع هو الوصول إليه.
subtitles.en: A hungry fox lived in a cave on a mountain.|A crow nested high among the rocks.|The fox thought the bird could reach food he could not reach.

subtitles.ar: ذهب الثعلب إلى الغراب وسلم عليه بلطف،|ثم قال: «نحن جاران منذ زمن طويل.|أتمنى أن نصبح صديقين وأن يساعد أحدنا الآخر».|لكنه كان يفكر في الطعام أكثر من الصداقة.
subtitles.en: The fox greeted the crow warmly|and proposed friendship|and mutual help.|But food, not friendship, was foremost in his mind.

subtitles.ar: نظر الغراب إليه بحذر وقال:|«أنت حيوان يصطاد الطيور، وأنا طائر قد أصبح فريستك.|كيف أطمئن إليك؟|لا تكفي الكلمات الجميلة حتى أصدق نيتك».
subtitles.en: The crow answered cautiously:|“You hunt birds, and I could become your prey.|How can I trust you?|Pleasant words cannot prove your intentions.”

subtitles.ar: لم يتراجع الثعلب.|قال إن الصداقة تنفع الجميع، ووعد بأن يكون جارًا مخلصًا.|ثم حكى قصة برغوث ساعدته فأرة،|فرد لها الجميل وساعدها على أخذ نقود من بيت تاجر.
subtitles.en: The fox insisted|that friendship benefits everyone.|He told of a flea sheltered by a mouse|who later repaid the favor by helping her take a merchant’s coins.

subtitles.ar: استمع الغراب إلى القصة، لكنه لم يقتنع.|أجاب: «قد يساعد الصديق صديقه،|لكنك خدعت ذئبًا عاش معك من قبل.|إذا لم تحفظ صداقته، فكيف أحفظ أنا نفسي بالقرب منك؟»
subtitles.en: The crow listened but was unconvinced.|“Friends may help one another,” he said,|“but you betrayed a wolf who lived with you.|How could I be safe near you?”

subtitles.ar: ثم حكى الغراب عن صقر كان يظلم الطيور بقوته.|وعندما كبر وضعف، صار يخدعها ليأكل من طعامها.|قال الغراب: «أخشى أن تكون صداقتك مثل حيلة ذلك الصقر».
subtitles.en: The crow told of a powerful falcon who oppressed other birds,|then when old and weak resorted to trickery to take their food.|“Your offer reminds me of him,” he said.

subtitles.ar: ذكر الغراب أيضًا عصفورًا حاول تقليد نسر قوي، فوقع في مشكلة كبيرة.|ثم قال للثعلب: «من الأفضل أن تعرف حدود قوتك،|وأن تبتعد عن عشي. لن أترك حذري بسبب وعودك».
subtitles.en: The crow also recalled a sparrow ruined by trying to imitate an eagle.|He warned the fox to respect his limits|and stay away from the nest.

subtitles.ar: فقد الثعلب الأمل في كسب الغراب، وابتعد وهو يظهر الحزن والغضب.|سأله الغراب عن سبب ذلك،|فأجابه بأنه وجده أشد مكرًا منه.|ثم عاد الثعلب وحده إلى كهفه.
subtitles.en: The fox lost hope and left, looking upset.|When the crow asked why,|the fox replied that the crow was craftier than himself.|He returned alone to his cave.

owner_questions: The script only says the flea helped the mouse take a merchant's coins; I show the traditional way (the flea bites the sleeping merchant, who hops away scratching, and the mouse takes one coin). Default: shown this way, comic and harmless.

The script only says the fox deceived a wolf who lived with him; I show the fox creeping away with their shared bone while the wolf sleeps (not the pit of the original tale). Default: the bone version.

The script only says the sparrow fell into big trouble copying an eagle; I show the traditional version softened: the eagle carries off a lamb (unharmed, surprised), the sparrow gets his feet stuck in a sheep's wool; no shepherd, no capture. Default: this version.

Additions beyond the script: the fox's growling belly (three times, including the last image), his hunter shadow on the rock, his tongue slipping out, and a heart that stands for his offer of friendship (burst by the crow, later sinking into the chasm). Default: all kept.

Invented English lettering: GRRR..., NEST, TOO HIGH!, POP!, TRUST ME!, OUCH!, SWISH!, SAFE HERE, MINE!, SAME TRICK, STUCK!, YOUR LIMIT, KEEP OUT!, WHY?, CRAFTIER!, LATER..., THE END. Default: all used (17 items; cut TRUST ME!, SWISH! and MINE! first if a leaner look is wanted).

The crow is played as a mother on a nest with three eggs (the script says only 'her nest' / 'my nest'), and is referred to as 'she' in the plan although the English text says 'he'. Default: eggs shown, no gendered lettering on screen.
implementation_notes: World is 1000 x 2300 (not the template's 1230 high): set WH = 2300 and clamp the camera with it. Two working zones: the top (terrace ground y 900, as in the template) and the foot (ground y 2100). Only S1 (crane), S2 and S12 use the foot.

Draw the sky with skyCycle in panel space before the world transform (so it fills any camera position), with u keyed by kfn: 0 s 0.12, 61 s 0.25, 144 s 0.38, 160.7 s 0.38, 161.2 s 0.46. Tint the rock a little warmer with dayCycle(u).warm.
Set LIFE.t = t each frame for automatic blinks; characters with an explicit lid need hand blinks (Math.max(lid, blink(t, seed))).
Every cue time in the JSON is the start of the named word in timing.json; use w(p, n) or the literal times. Anticipation starts up to 0.4 s before the cue where an action says so.

Story clouds use the Library thoughtCloud for told tales as well as thoughts: yellow fill for the fox's private thoughts (S2, S3), paper for told tales (S6, S8, S9), blue with a halftone wash for the crow's memory of the wolf (S7). Tail always to the teller's head or beak. Clouds stay in the upper left; they must never cover the fox's or the crow's face. Figures inside at least 110 px on screen (use scale 0.5 to 0.55 and oversize the flea).
The fox faces right (dir 1) in the top zone except when he walks away (S11) and in S12 (dir -1). Use turnFlip for every turn. All walks through walk(posFn, t) with footfalls for dust; no sliding.
Gap discipline: the fox's toes never pass x 600 and the crow never leaves the pinnacle; the chasm stays visible in every two-shot. It is the picture of the crow's caution.
Mask on / mask off (guide section 9): the fox's flat face appears only when his head is turned from the crow (36.7-41.2) and in the peek at 70.3.

Sound: narration is the soundtrack. Effects only at the listed times, all in real pauses (3.48-4.24, 11.82-12.38, 20.36-21.54, 41.20-42.70, 55.86-56.34, after 164.56); master 0.6. From 42.7 to 164.5 there are almost no gaps: the comic lettering there is silent.
Lettering: Bangers, labels at least 28 px and headlines at least 44 px at 1280x720 scale, never over a face; no dashes.
Panel-only shake is not needed except a 2-frame, 3-unit bump when the edge crumbles (137.28) and on the angry stamp (152.04).

warnings: Paragraphs 3 to 8 are almost continuous speech (no pause of 0.6 s after 42.7 s), so nearly all sound effects sit in the first 43 s and at the very end. Do not add effects under the words.

This is a talking story: two characters stand still for two minutes. The plan keeps it moving with three story clouds, the heart, the shadow and the gap; if the clouds are cut or simplified the film will go static.
S6 packs a whole inset story into 8.5 s (73.8-82.3); it must be staged very simply (one floor line, left to right) or it will not read on a phone.
The hawk kind, rat and insect are planned by other stories but not in the Library yet; if they are built first elsewhere, use those drawings and names.
The crane in S1 passes 1060 world units in 2.5 s; keep the rock face detail sparse so it does not strobe at 30 fps.
Time of day moves from morning to dusk across one conversation; this is a mood device, not narrated. The single LATER card is at 160.75-161.55 over the words 'then he returned'.
